requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas` skill whose description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project, naming as signs of one a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{cite}` references in code.
rationale:
`requirements.cli.overview_skill` has three obligations. Habeas bundles a `habeas` skill. Its description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project. That description names four signs of such a project.

The test `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_is_used_at_the_start_of_any_work_in_a_habeas_project]` is marked `{test}` for the requirement. It covers all three obligations:
- **Bundling:** it reads the `habeas` skill through the helpers `description`, `skill_md` and `skill_files`. `skill_files` embeds `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` with `include_str!`, so the test fails to compile if the skill is not bundled. It also panics if the front matter has no `description:` line.
- **Timing:** it asserts the description starts with "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas".
- **Signs:** it asserts the description contains each of the four signs: ``a `habeas` dev-dependency``, ``a `habeas.toml` ``, ``` `{req}` directives in its mdBook ```, and ``` `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references in code ```. The last one covers all three reference kinds.

These assertions enforce the clauses. A description that omitted any sign or dropped the start-of-work instruction would fail.

The helpers are reached from the marked test, so they need no markers of their own. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_are_five_skill_directories_each_home_to_its_topics]` separately checks which skill files are listed. I found no unresolved gaps.
